name: Chalcolepidius smaragdinus
intro: I kept a female in August 2021. Its metallic color comes from scale-like hairs, and both color and striping vary among adults.

facts.title: Container
facts.text: One US gallon (3.8 L), well ventilated

facts.title: Floor
facts.text: 1.3 in (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber with bark flats

sections.title: Adults
sections.text: I housed the female in a ventilated one-gallon tub (3.8 L) with 1.3 inches (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber and flat bark for cover. I did not record eggs from this female. For a laying trial I would offer bark and folded paper towel, the two surfaces on which our Chalcolepidius webbi laid eggs.

sources.title: My two adult housing trials, August 2021
Museum of Comparative Zoology, Arizona specimen

gallery.caption: Chalcolepidius cf. smaragdinus feeding at a sap flow, August 2, 2025. The species identification is provisional.
gallery.alt: A metallic green click beetle with violet-blue legs feeding on exposed sap.

native_status.text: Casari recorded this species in Arizona, New Mexico and Sonora, Mexico. The type series includes a specimen from the Gila Valley, Arizona.

sources.title: Museum of Comparative Zoology, Arizona specimen

distribution.caption: Casari records Arizona and New Mexico in the United States and Sonora in Mexico.
distribution.alt: Documented regions for Chalcolepidius smaragdinus: Arizona, New Mexico, Sonora.
